subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw accept managed per-agent plugin installs now, and what lifecycle/security contract must exist before exposing `plugins install --agent`?
rationale: This changes public CLI behavior, persisted plugin install records, plugin code roots, discovery/update/uninstall behavior, and agent trust boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Complete lifecycle contract before merge
options.body: Define and implement scoped install identity across install, uninstall, update, registry/index metadata, discovery, doctor, docs, and security proof before exposing the flag.

options.title: Pause for product/security review
options.body: Keep the branch open but blocked while maintainers decide whether managed per-agent plugin installs belong in core and what guarantees they need.

options.title: Reject install scoping for now
options.body: Close or redirect this PR to the canonical issue if maintainers prefer existing workspace plugins, `plugins.load.paths`, or future per-agent config as the isolation path.

recommendation.title: Complete lifecycle contract before merge
recommendation.body: Define and implement scoped install identity across install, uninstall, update, registry/index metadata, discovery, doctor, docs, and security proof before exposing the flag.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans plugin lifecycle, config compatibility, and agent workspace boundaries where recent history points most strongly to this owner.
